subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Hooke's Law: How Springs Push Back
description: Learn Hooke's Law: How Springs Push Back in one minute.

hook.text: Press a spring and it pushes back. Press twice as hard and it pushes back exactly twice as much.

buildup.text: Robert Hooke discovered this in 1660. Force equals spring constant times displacement. F equals kx.

discovery.text: The spring constant k tells you stiffness. A car spring has a high k. A pen spring has a low one.

twist.text: Push too far and the spring deforms permanently. Beyond the elastic limit, Hooke's law breaks down.

climax.text: Hooke's law governs mattresses, trampolines, shock absorbers, and every spring in every machine.

punchline.text: Push a spring. It remembers. Push too far. It forgets.

quiz.question: What does Hooke's law state about springs?
options: Springs lose energy proportionally to how fast they are compressed
Force is proportional to displacement within the elastic limit
All springs have the same stiffness regardless of material
